questions.stem: An experiment using a spirit burner gives an enthalpy of combustion value that is lower than the literature value. What is the most likely reason?

options.text: Heat was lost to the surroundings during the experiment
The water was too hot at the start
Too much fuel was burned in the experiment

questions.explanation: The most common source of error in calorimetry experiments is heat loss to the surroundings. Not all the heat from combustion goes into the water; some is lost to the air, the container, and by evaporation. This means the measured temperature rise is smaller than it should be, giving a lower calculated enthalpy value.
